To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the implementation of the MSP in Germany was associated with an increase in BCS rates in women < 50 and ≥ 50 years and with a decrease in MET rates in women aged 50+ years.
the introduction of the MSP was accompanied by a shift from MET to BCS in the screening-eligible population and in the oldest population.

there was a strong increase in breast-conserving surgery (BCS) rates in women with invasive and in situ breast cancer in the screening-eligible and the non-screening-eligible age groups during and after the implementation and full-running of the nationwide mammography screening program in Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the German MSP on surgery rates for breast cancer.
the effect of the nationwide mammography screening program in Germany on breast cancer surgery.
the impact of the German MSP on breast cancer treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a clear shift towards BCS in women with invasive breast cancer, but also a considerable increase in BCS and MET in women with in situ breast cancer.
the MSP in Germany did not lead to a substantial increase of breast cancer surgery rates.
the implementation of MSP has not led to a general increase of breast cancer surgery rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the implementation of the MSP in Germany was followed by a strong shift towards breast-conserving surgery for invasive breast cancer among women aged 70 years or older and women aged 50-69 years, who are eligible for screening.
the MSP in Germany led to a shift in breast cancer treatment from MET to BCS.

the implementation of a nationwide population-based mammographic screening program in Germany led to a shift from MET to BCS in the age group of 50–69 years and to a considerable increase of BCS for women aged > 70 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of the MSP in Germany led to a strong increase of BCS rates in the screening-eligible women and in the elderly women.
the MSP has led to a substantial increase in BCS rates for women with invasive breast cancer, especially in the screening-eligible population.
the implementation of a nationwide MSP is followed by a shift from MET to BCS for invasive and in situ breast cancer in Germany.
